text:
Parker Wotherspoon had to work for this. A fourth-round pick in 2015, he spent years in the AHL before finally sticking in the NHL, and last season in Pittsburgh he put up 30 points in 80 games. Evolving-Hockey had him 72nd of 215 defensemen with 500-plus minutes, worth about one win above replacement.

Now in Vegas, he opened the season playing 15 to 20 minutes a night before landing on injured reserve. The Golden Knights activated him on Nov. 11, according to Daily Faceoff, and he played 15.5 minutes in the win over Utah that night.

Seven games in, he has no points, but the underlying play is good. Vegas has taken 59% of five-on-five shot attempts and 56.7% of expected goals with him on the ice, and it has scored 5.2 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That kind of gap tends to close. Watch how quickly he gets back to the minutes he had before the injury.
headline: Wotherspoon is back from injured reserve
